newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA'S CURCIC APOLOGISES FOR OUTBURST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA'S CURCIC APOLOGISES FOR OUTBURST.

text.p: Sasa Curcic has apologised to Aston Villa manager Brian Little for a weekend outburst in which he described his decision to join the English premier league side as "the biggest mistake I have made in my life".
The Serb midfielder, who said he wanted to leave Villa after spending the last eight matches on the substitutes' bench, has sent a letter of regret to Little and hopes to resolve the dispute.

"I have received a faxed letter from Sasa apologising for his words at the weekend," Little confirmed. "He apologised for the distress he has caused and also apologised to the chairman, supporters and the club."
"He says he is now prepared to discuss a positive and constructive way forward. It looks as though he realises that he did something wrong."

Curcic, who joined Villa from first division Bolton less than five months ago for four million pounds ($6.7 million), could now replace injured midfielder Mark Draper in the side to face championship rivals Newcastle on Saturday.
Little, who had to deal with dressing room discontent from defenders Paul McGrath and Carl Tiler earlier in the season, insisted all was well at Villa Park.

"I've not got a problem with my dressing room and we won't have one," he said. "People do knock on my door quite a few times about this and that but we keep things very much in-house and, whatever the problems of the last few days, that situation will return.
